More about the Zinc Venture Builder | Zinc Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team More about the Zinc Venture Builder Find out more details about the Zinc Venture Builder – from what a successful Zinc Founder looks like to how the Venture Builder might work for you as an international Founder or Woman in Tech. What does a successful Zinc Founder look like? Zinc brings together cohorts of 70 entrepreneurs , for each Venture Builder. Those who join the Venture Builder are talented individuals, from around the world who are ready to commit to building a new scalable, mission-led business, from scratch. They are all united by the specific mission the Venture Builder is aimed at solving. Based on experience in backing over 200 founders to date, we put together a list of the attributes we know make a good fit with our Venture Builder and successful Zinc founders. There isn’t one specific template of what a Zinc Founder looks like. However, there are universal characteristics that we assess potential applicants on and look for across each mission: Mission-drive Successful founders at Zinc are fully committed to tackling the mission for the Venture Builder. Catalyst | Zinc Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team UKRI Healthy Ageing Catalyst Awards Zinc and UKRI are proud to be partnering for the fourth round of the UKRI Healthy Ageing Catalyst Awards. This programme is not currently open for applications. Applicants who have submitted an expression of interest can find the guidance documents here . Info for applicants Catalyst Awards Fourth Cohort Since the first call for the Healthy Ageing Catalyst Awards in 2020, Zinc and UKRI have partnered to fund entrepreneurial academics who want to translate their research into impactful and scalable products, services and interventions. The Awards are part of the UKRI Healthy Ageing Challenge and the Healthy Longevity Global Grand Challenge, founded by the U.S. National Academy of Medicine. This is a worldwide movement to improve physical, mental, and social well-being for people as they age. In 2023, Zinc will support its fourth cohort of researchers to create innovations that: Allow everyone to remain active, productive, independent and socially connected across generations for as long as possible; Narrow the gap between the experiences of the richest and the poorest. Guidance documents £62,500 in funding and a dedicated programme of support UKRI award successful applicants up to £62,500 (fEC) (80%

Guidance documents £62,500 in funding and a dedicated programme of support UKRI award successful applicants up to £62,500 (fEC) (80% from UKRI, 20% contribution from your host institution) and Zinc offer a comprehensive and proven programme of enterprise support, which will help you scale the impact of your research and explore different pathways to impact.

Building on the success of our Prototyping Problems workshops in 2021 and 2022, these workshops with brand-new content will offer inspiration from current and previous Awards winners alongside practical advice about submitting your expression of interest.

Final decisions June A decision will then be made on the cohort of Catalyst Awards holders for the 2023/24 academic year, who will undertake Zinc’s programme of support and receive up to £62,500 in funding.

Formal Submission Once you have been selected for the Awards (and so offered UKRI funding and a place on the Zinc programme of support) you will be required to submit details of your application through the UKRI Je-S system.

This programme is designed to unite researchers from across the social sciences and biosciences to cross-pollinate skills, ideas, and expertise to build exciting new ventures. Participants will come together to address a shared challenge: How to build healthy, sustainable, and resilient food systems . You can learn more about programme eligibility criteria here . APPLICATIONS CLOSED The Challenge As the global population approaches 10 billion and climate change is increasingly impacting food security, the pressure on our food systems is intensifying. The core purpose of our food systems is to provide enough nutrition to meet global dietary needs – yet this system is under intense threat, compounded by declining soil quality, reduced biodiversity, water stress, the proliferation of crop disease and supply chain disruptions. Without urgent and radical transformation, we risk pushing our food systems beyond key planetary boundaries. Pioneer | Zinc Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team The Academy The Zinc Academy is the education arm of Zinc and focuses on accelerating the impact of mission-driven individuals. Combining diverse talent with a common mission, the Academy launches changemakers along a variety of routes to impact. The Academy is currently running two part-time programmes: Pioneer and Catalyst. More information on the pioneer programme in mental health can be found below, and for more details of the Catalyst programme for researchers interested in healthy ageing, please click here . Overview For those driven by the Mission of Mental Health, but frustrated by their current level of impact. For those that know they can do more, but don’t know where to start. For those that want to create a game-plan alongside their current role. Zinc is on a mission to mobilise talent to tackle the world’s most important problems, and to generate maximum impact. Now, we are going further. We have recruited 30 impact-driven people to take part in our first Pioneer Programme. The Pioneer Programme accelerates the impact of those individuals who want to contribute other system-level solutions to Zinc’s missions. It’s a place for changemakers – from healthcare professionals to policymakers, charity workers to entrepreneurs,

It’s a place for changemakers – from healthcare professionals to policymakers, charity workers to entrepreneurs, researchers to creative designers – who are passionate about making progress on complex problems.
And we are starting with Mental Health.

During our 9 month part-time programme, the cohort of pioneers will be exposed to the best in mental health learning and expertise, meet a powerful network of speakers and Fellows, be connected to unique placements and a portfolio of mental health start-ups, and build connections with a cohort of like minded individuals.

Current programme dates: September 2020 – June 2021 ARE YOU AN EMPLOYER Programme Content In-depth Mental Health Curriculum – including exploration of science & interventions, discovering individual characteristics and the wider landscape and issues in society.
Timeline The programme is split into three 3-month phases – Open & Discover, Inspire & Design and Embed & Change: Open & Discover Be exposed to a radical and comprehensive mental health curriculum.
Inspire & Design Build connections with successful innovators inside the mental health space and take part in creative workshops to focus your interest and design your plan.
Embed & Change Activate your plan alongside the sustained support of an Executive Coach, a Mental Health Mentor, the Zinc Team, and your fellow Cohort.

Research & Development at Zinc | Zinc Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team Our Mission Investment Portfolio Innovation Partners News Team Research & Development at Zinc Our Mission We exist to find, scale and share new ways of combining high-quality research with innovative product development, in order to tackle at scale the most important problems within Zinc’s missions: improving mental health, unlocking opportunities for people in places hard-hit by globalisation and automation; improving the quality of later life; and reducing the harm people do to the environment. Zinc R&D is a hub for innovators and researchers who want to accelerate their impact, combine complementary skills, and use research knowledge and methods to create applied, impactful solutions. Our Approach We are an interdisciplinary team of applied researchers and scientists, committed to building a new approach to science-based innovation. Our approach to product development combines the best of creative design, scientific rigour and entrepreneurship, in an environment that is untethered by traditional disciplinary and sectoral silos. We connect the research and innovation systems: leveraging and translating existing evidence, empowering a diverse range of user groups to co-create solutions, experimenting with innovative methods, and generating and sharing new knowledge.
